cohort: The study included 155 deaths of children under 5 years of age interviewed from all households (30,857) in selected urban slum areas in Bangladesh, identified through the Urban Health and Demographic Surveillance System.
finding: The major leading causes of under-5 deaths in this slum area were birth asphyxia, pneumonia, and infectious diseases, with birth asphyxia being the most common cause in the neonatal period.
mod_finding: The cause of mortality fraction varied by delivery-related attributes, including the mode and place of delivery.
birth_weight: low birth weights were identified as a cause of death for 6.5% of children
gest_age: prematurity was identified as a cause of death for 6.5% of children
